hive: 🐝 Good day, sir. Dabba Days is set up on your computer and ready, though nothing has been built yet. What shall we build first?
We haven't met properly yet. Say "set me up" and I'll get to know your business or your product in about two minutes, or help you start something new.
🐝 Let's get you set up. First, which of these is you?
Very good. 5 quick steps, about two minutes. Say skip to any, or stop to carry on later; I keep everything as you go.

1 of 5. Your business.
What is it called, what does it do, and who are your customers? A line or two is plenty (🎙 a voice note works too).
✅ Got it, Dabba Days: Home cooks make lunch and we deliver it to office workers. We deliver Monday to Friday. Our customers are people working in offices.

2 of 5. Where it runs.
Where can I see it? Send its web address.

3 of 5. Numbers and data.
I already have the code here (15 files). So I can answer things like "how many orders this week?", send me any of these, as many as you like:
• an admin or analytics address, with its key
• a database address (please a read-only login)
• a shared spreadsheet link, or a CSV or Excel file

I only ever read; I never change your data. Keys stay on this computer. Say done when finished.

✅ dabba database: I can see 8 tables: complaints, cooks, customers, deliveries, payments, payouts, plans, subscriptions.

Anything else? Or say done.

4 of 5. How you run things.
Anything written down: policies, FAQ, price list, a pitch deck? Send the files here (PDF, text, CSV), or tell me in a few lines. Say done when finished.
📚 Read: 13 things kept, and 7 rules for how the product behaves. Anything else, or done?

5 of 5. Hosting.
Vercel, Netlify, Render, Railway, Fly or Azure? Or say don't know.

✅ All set, Dabba Days. I know 18 things about your business; read-only access to dabba database.

From now on, just tell me what you want. For example:
• "how many orders this week?"
• "show me the pricing page on desktop"
• "I want more repeat buyers"
• "add a referral page"

I'll ask only what I can't work out myself: your own rules for the unusual cases.

🐝 Sir, cooks get ₹70 for each lunch they make, paid every Monday for the week before. Your payout records show this happens every week.

One thing your policy doesn't say: a cook with no complaints in a month gets an extra ₹500, paid with that month's last weekly payout. Is that your rule? I can add it to the policy.

plan.title: A shorter sign-up form with GST optional
plan.why: Sign-up asks for 9 things, all required, including a company GST number most office workers don't have, so many can't finish; making GST and desk number optional lets them pay and start.
plan.seen: signup.html: 9 fields, among them 'Company GST number' and 'Floor and desk number', with the note 'All fields are required. Your first month is charged today.'
plan.build: In signup.html, keep name, email, phone, company name, office address, area and plan as required (add the `required` attribute). Mark 'Company GST number' as '(optional, only if you want a company invoice)' and 'Floor and desk number' as '(optional)', without `required`. Change the note to 'Fields marked optional can be left blank. Your first month is charged today.' Keep the field names, area list, plan list and button. In test_dabba.py add test_signup_gst_optional: read signup.html and check that the gst input has no `required` attribute and that name, email, phone and address do.

plan.title: Show price per lunch and what's protected
plan.why: The Plans page shows only a monthly total and says nothing about skip credit, unpaid pauses, holidays or missed-lunch refunds, so a first-time buyer can't tell what one lunch costs or what happens on days they're away.
plan.seen: plans.html: '₹2,400 / month' etc., with only 'Every plan is 20 lunches a month... Billed monthly.' index.html says only 'Skip a lunch and get credit' with no amount. The rules exist only on skip.html and pause.html, which are reached from My account, and in billing.py (SKIP_CREDIT_RS=100, MAX_PAUSE_
plan.build: In billing.py add price_per_lunch(plan_price_rs) returning plan_price_rs // LUNCHES_PER_MONTH, and have refund_for_missed_lunch use it. In plans.html, under each monthly price, add a muted line: 'That's ₹120 a lunch' / '₹150 a lunch' / '₹170 a lunch'. Below the cards, add a card 'What you're covered for' with: 'Skip a lunch before 9 pm the night before: ₹100 off your next bill.'; 'Pause up to 10 days a month. Paused days aren't charged.'; 'No lunch and no charge on Karnataka public holidays.'; 'If your cook is sick we send another cook from your area. If no one can cook, that lunch is refunded in full.'; 'A missing lunch is always refunded.' On index.html change 'Skip a lunch and get credit.' to 'Skip before 9 pm the night before and get ₹100 off your next bill.' Keep the existing prices. In test_dabba.py add tests: price_per_lunch(2400)==120, (3000)==150, (3400)==170, and plans.html contains '₹120', '₹150', '₹170', '9 pm', '10 days' and 'public holidays'.

plan.title: A one-week trial before the full month
plan.why: Sign-up charges a whole month today before the customer has tasted anything, a big first step for one office worker; a week of 5 lunches lets them try it before committing.
plan.seen: signup.html: 'Your first month is charged today.' and a 'Pay and subscribe' button with no smaller option. plans.html offers only monthly plans. You said there's no trial now but you'd be open to a cheap trial week.
plan.build: In billing.py add TRIAL_LUNCHES = 5 and trial_week_price(plan_price_rs) returning the trial amount you choose (if it's the normal rate, price_per_lunch(plan_price_rs) * TRIAL_LUNCHES). In signup.html add a 'Start with' choice: 'A trial week (5 lunches)' or 'A full month (20 lunches)', and show the amount charged today for the chosen plan. When trial is picked, change the note to 'Your trial week is charged today. After it, you can carry on monthly or stop.' On plans.html add a line above the Subscribe button: 'Not sure? Try a week first: 5 lunches for ₹X.' using your amounts per plan. Keep the existing monthly prices and all skip/pause rules. In test_dabba.py, test trial_week_price for all 3 plans and check that signup.html and plans.html mention 'trial week'.
plan.decide: What should a trial week (5 lunches) cost?
options: A cheaper first week, e.g. ₹500 for any plan
